about_p1: I grew up in Lofoten, and my interest in electronics started early, with my dad as the biggest source of inspiration. The road here was still a bit winding: sports studies in upper secondary school, military service in the King's Guard, six months as a substitute teacher, then a preparatory science course, then a bachelor in electronic systems design at NTNU. I think that road is why I am good at explaining. I remember well what it is like not to understand it yet. My time in the military, in the King's Guard 3rd Company, taught me discipline, order and precision, which I bring into my engineering work.
about_p2: Alongside my studies I have been a class representative, sat on reference groups and taken on leadership roles. I like making things run smoothly for others, whether it is a course or a training group.
about_p3: I speak Norwegian, English and Arabic, and have a connection to the Arabic language and Iraqi culture.
step2_d: Analog electronics, filter design, radio communication
contact_text: I am looking for a summer job in 2027 within electronics and embedded systems. Feel free to reach out if you have something on your mind.
p1_title: Object detection for the blind and visually impaired
p1_text: A wearable aid that finds fruit with a camera and shows the direction with a vibration belt and Norwegian speech. I was responsible for the software.
p2_text: Analog interface circuit, an ESP32 that computes heart rate and a live view in the browser, from breadboard to a four-layer PCB.
p3_text: Synchronous buck converter with the LTC3807 holding the output within ±30 mV. Two PCB revisions, where the first failed because of a wiring error.
p4_text: Drivers for GPIO, I2C, SPI and USART written from scratch in C, without HAL, with example programs.
repo1_text: The software for the aid for the blind: object detection, speech and control of the vibration belt.
repo2_text: Register-level drivers for the STM32F411RE and examples from blinking an LED to I2C and SPI towards an Arduino.
